question: Among the four given pairs of gears, which one is likely to last longer over time?
initial_trace_steps: To determine which pair of gears will last longer, we need to consider the common factors of the number of teeth in each gear pair. Gears with fewer common factors will have less repetitive contact between the same teeth, reducing wear and tear over time.
For the pair of gears with 16 and 9 teeth, the only common factor is 1, meaning they have no other common divisors.
For the pair of gears with 12 and 8 teeth, the common factors are {1,2,4}, they have two common divisors.
For the pair of gears with 18 and 12 teeth, the common factors are {1,2,3}, they have two common divisors.
For the pair of gears with 14 and 7 teeth, the common factors are {1,7}, they have one common divisor.
For the pair of gears with 20 and 15 teeth, the common factors are {1,5}, they have one common divisor.
As a result, the gear pair with 16 and 9 teeth is likely to last longer compared to other pairs with more common factors, as it minimizes repetitive contact and wear.

Applying that rule to the options: gcd(16,9)=1, gcd(20,15)=5, gcd(18,12)=6, gcd(12,8)=4, and gcd(14,7)=7. So only 16 and 9 are relatively prime; every other pair has a common factor greater than 1 and would repeat tooth contact sooner.
Therefore the pair most likely to last longer over time is A, 16 and 9, because it is the only option whose tooth counts are coprime under the rule grounded by the instructional OCR.
